what: MESH_PLAN step 0 / §2b, run live: node A sends three signed cards to node B over a real WebRTC DataChannel; B judges each one itself.
honest_scope: Two independent browser nodes on ONE machine (different origins, so separate storage and separate Ed25519 keys). A recorded observation, not a regenerable receipt: browser keys are random. The byte-reproducible receipt is receipts/edge-verify.json (CI re-runs it). The two-DEVICE run waits on a second device.

nodeA.grew: 0.820498 (in the browser, on its own copy of the data)

topology.link: RTCPeerConnection DataChannel, invite + reply pasted by hand (fall-os webrtc.mjs, fall-federate invite check)
topology.stun: none — the STUN box was unticked; no third party at all
topology.pairing: B replied, then A connected 25 s later; B received the cards 62 s after replying (the 20 s guest timeout that lost every card in the first run is fixed: the listener is attached when the link is created)

network: node A requested only http://localhost:8150 (page, modules, its data); node B only http://127.0.0.1:8150 plus blob: URLs (decoding the received pictures locally). Zero requests left the machine.
transport: each card travelled as a PNG picture in 6 chunks; B reassembled it, checked its sha256 against the sender's, then read the signed envelope off the pixels

cases.reason: reproduced 0.820498 here — the signature proves who, the re-run proved what
seal mismatch — the Ed25519 signature does not cover these bytes
the claim does not reproduce — the card says 0.900000, the re-run here gives 0.820498

rule: a signature proves who; only a re-run on the receiving node proves what
